synopsis: Required detection range is reliable sensing distance calculated backwards from stopping distance, all detection/decision/actuation delays, clearance and sensor error; it varies with speed, grade, load, surface and delay and must be achieved in every approved operating condition [f13987, f13993]. ISO 21815-3:2023 structures avoidance distance around detection, determination and action, stopping and a safety distance, while the booklet's engineering equation adds a machine-envelope offset and is explicitly not a verbatim ISO equation [f7007, f7010]. MOSH specifies a minimum 200 m surface-machine detection range, whereas US surface-coal rules require enough sensing range for an endangered person to escape without specifying metres; a separate 40 t example at 15 km/h on a 10% downgrade requires at least 9.5 m before sensor-error allowance, not a replacement for those regulatory requirements [f13995, f2622, f13656]. If degraded sensing falls below the required stopping range, braking models cannot restore the lost margin, so speed may need limiting; weather-aware sensor models should therefore feed detection delay, range and error into braking simulation [f6585, f11330, f6487]. Prototype correlation tests should precede the scenario matrix when the prototype arrives in mid-2027, and a sensor change in 2027 would invalidate detection-range evidence and sensor correlation; the claimed coverage of “100+ job-site types” remains unsupported without a taxonomy connecting sites to sensing and stopping variables [f744, f11912, f8214].
